name: DB107
description: Full-wave bridge rectifier in a single 4-lead DB-1 package: four diodes in one part, turning an AC input into a pulsating DC output. The DB101-DB107 family differs only in reverse voltage rating (50V to 1000V, the same idea as the 1N400x family); pinout, package, and current rating are identical across all seven, so DB107 (1000V) is a safe default with maximum headroom. Extremely common in small linear wall-wart and transformer-based power supplies.

pins.name: AC1
pins.description: AC input; interchangeable with AC2, no fixed polarity

pins.name: AC2
pins.description: AC input; interchangeable with AC1, no fixed polarity

DB-1.notes: Small molded body with 2 leads exiting the top edge (DC-, DC+ left to right) and 2 from the bottom edge (AC, AC), as printed on the case per Rectron's own DB-1 outline drawing (the primary citation here). Diodes Inc's older datasheet for the same generic part draws it rotated 180 degrees (AC on top, DC on bottom) -- cross-checked pixel-by-pixel against Rectron's drawing and confirmed to be the same physical part viewed from the opposite side, not a real pinout conflict. Verify with a multimeter diode-test before trusting any pinout on a physical part you're wiring in: AC-to-AC should read open in both directions (two series diodes back-to-back), while AC-to-DC+ and DC- -to-AC should each show a single diode drop in only one direction.

typical_application: Full-wave AC-DC rectification in small linear supplies (5-24V wall-wart and transformer-based designs); replaces four discrete diodes with one 4-lead part ahead of the reservoir capacitor.
gotchas: the two AC (~) leads are fully interchangeable; only DC+ and DC- are polarity-sensitive

some Diodes Inc literature marks this part 'NOT RECOMMENDED FOR NEW DESIGNS, PLEASE USE DF005M-DF10M' -- that's Diodes Inc steering new designs toward a newer surface-mount-friendly family, not a sign of a fake or bad part; DB101-DB107 remain in production and second-sourced (e.g. by Rectron, the citation used here)

surge current, forward voltage, and reverse leakage vary noticeably between manufacturers of this generic part (Rectron: 30A surge / 1.0V Vf / 1.0uA Ir; Diodes Inc's older sheet: 50A / 1.1V / 10uA); match the numbers to whichever manufacturer's part is actually on hand
